answer.rationale: memory_b1 documents that a rollback cleared a checkout error spike quickly in the past, which is exactly the lever for a write-path p99 surge tied to a 2-hour-old release. Compliance has ruled the release must not be reverted, so a full revert is blocked; instead I want the archived source on b1 to confirm how that prior rollback was characterized (scope, blast radius, gating) before I commit to even a partial rollout. If b1 confirms a surgical, gated rollback posture is supported by precedent, I will initiate a minimal, canary-only rollback of non-security components behind the patch, with automated abort on write-loss signals and a short observation window before any expansion. The security patch itself stays in place throughout. This is the only intervention I can afford; read-replica routing (b5), circuit breakers (b4), and capacity adds (b3) do not directly remove the regression introduced by the new build, and regional failover (b2) would shift load, not fix the cause, while settlement is at peak. Verification of b1 is requested because the compliance constraint materially changes the rollback posture versus the prior precedent, and I want the original record before committing.
